Part B
Situation
You are Nico Lin. You work for Shiny Diamond Lighting Ltd, a company that designs, makes and sells neon lighting products and services. Your work involves writing and editing texts for company use. Your boss, Floyd Mann, has asked you to do some tasks.
You will listen to a podcast of Wish You Were Here, an arts and culture radio programme on Hong Kong Radio. On the podcast you will hear Julia Din interview Pris Fong, owner of Shiny Diamond Lighting Ltd, and her chief designer and neon artist Rick Lai.
Before the recording is played, you will have five minutes to study the Question-Answer Book and the Data File to familiarise yourself with the situation and the tasks.
Complete the tasks by following the instructions in the Question-Answer Book and on the recording. You will find all the information you need in the Question-Answer Book, the Data File and on the recording. As you listen you can make notes on page 3 of the Data File.
You now have five minutes to familiarise yourself with the Question-Answer Book and the Data File.

To: Nico Lin
Sent: April 26 2022 10:18 AM
From: Floyd Mann
Subject: Things to do
Dear Nico,
Busy week I’m afraid. As Public Relations Officer, can you apply your magic with words and get onto the following things ASAP?
First, write an email to the students at the Hong Kong Design School to encourage them to apply to join Shiny Diamond Lighting Ltd as trainees. Write it so that it gets their interest and is clear about how they should apply. Listen to the Wish You Were Here podcast, and look at the company handbook and Rick Lai’s interview in the Hong Kong Arts and Crafts magazine for details.
Next, Pris wants us to make a how-to leaflet to be given out to customers when they visit our neon light factory. I have put in the pictures, but you will need to finish the text. Use full sentences and don’t use bullet points! Take a look at the company handbook and Rick Lai’s interview in the Hong Kong Arts and Crafts magazine.
Finally, we need to update the webpage for our products. Look at the inventory from the previous stock take and the company handbook. Rick Lai and Pris Fong also discuss some product details on the Wish You Were Here podcast.
I’ve noticed customers discussing our products in the Customer Comments section of our website. That might help you with some of these tasks. Rick Lai and Pris Fong were also discussing all of these tasks on the Management WhatsApp group — I’ll forward the messages to you.
Don’t blow a fuse!
Floyd Mann
General Manager

Messages from the Shiny Diamond Management WhatsApp Group — Chat 1
Shiny Diamond Management
FloydHi Nico! These are the messages about the Recruitment Email and the How-to Leaflet.
RickWe’re asking Nico to write the trainee recruitment email. What’s a good way to start the email? I mean, how can we attract the most creative candidates?
PrisBegin with a question. Get them curious.
RickWhat kind of question?
PrisHow about asking them if they enjoy making things with their hands?
RickGreat idea. That will make a big impact, right at the beginning of the email. And how do they apply?
PrisThey can simply reply to the recruitment email.
RickOf course! We should definitely include that. I have another question about the How-to Leaflet.
PrisShoot.
RickShould we mention where customers can hang their signs? In the “display” section, I mean.
PrisSure. They can hang the signs on a wall. Wait: where else do customers place their signs?
RickLet me check the Customer Comments.

Messages from Shiny Diamond Management WhatsApp Group — Chat 2
Shiny Diamond Management
FloydNico — these are the messages about the Webpage for Products. Thanks.
PrisOn the webpage, I’ve added a 10% discount on the Hong Kong Skyline design.
RickAre you sure you want to do that?
PrisYes — we need to get more interest in the product.
RickOK, we can. But it’ll reduce our profit.
PrisGood point. How about we only have the discount for the first 20 orders? That’ll get people more interested, but allow us to make money later.
RickOK, sounds good. Get Nico to add that to the section on price.
PrisSpeaking of which, did you get Nico to add an example answer for the FAQ on what messages customers can write?
RickNot yet. Was it “Love lives forever!” we were going to use?
PrisYes, that’s right. It’s our most popular message by far. Another FAQ is about the delivery time. Are we down to 1 month now?
RickEven better - we can deliver in around 3 weeks.
PrisOne more thing on the customer-designed signs. Does the webpage state which file format customers should use to upload their design?
RickI wasn’t sure, so I left it blank. It should be JPEG files, right?
PrisYes, and PNG files too.

Interview with Neon Master Rick Lai in Hong Kong Arts and Crafts Magazine
We spoke with Rick Lai, Hong Kong’s top lighting designer, who works for the award-winning Shiny Diamond Lighting Ltd.
Hong Kong Arts and Crafts:What do you enjoy most about your work?
Rick Lai:There are many aspects to the job I enjoy but what I love most is taking a customer’s design and turning it into a neon sign. It’s quite a complicated process. Basically, in the planning stage, when we receive the design, we use a grid.
Hong Kong Arts and Crafts:Why do you do that?
Rick Lai:We use it to decide how many glass tubes we need. That’s all before we start making the sign using a machine called the Glass Heater.
Hong Kong Arts and Crafts:What does that do?
Rick Lai:We use it to bend the glass tubes. We then have another machine which cleans the glass tubes.
Hong Kong Arts and Crafts:How does it get them clean?
Rick Lai:It uses electricity. Shocking, right? Also, whenever we move the glass tubes, they can be broken very easily so we have to be very, very careful with them. That’s the boring part for me, because I like to work quickly! Finally, we are also very careful to test if the tubes are working before we move on to the display stage. One time, a customer returned a faulty sign. It was so embarrassing!
Hong Kong Arts and Crafts:What is the future for lighting design in Hong Kong?
Rick Lai:It’s very bright! We are looking for trainees at the moment, so if any of your readers are interested, please apply to be a trainee.
Hong Kong Arts and Crafts:How can they apply?
Rick Lai:The instructions will be in recruitment emails we are sending out soon. One thing to pay attention to, though: applicants must send us 4 or 5 photos of their previous work. That way, we can really get a feel for their ability.
